label: Formulated and introduced The Banality of Evil
description: Hannah Arendt formulated and introduced the concept of "The Banality of Evil", which became a seminal contribution in ethics philosophy.
dialecticalTension: Formulating an epistemic apparatus to resolve central problems in ethics.
historicalContext: Introduced during the Contemporary & Post-Structural as part of Hannah Arendt's canonical writings.

label: Reversed Heidegger's being-toward-death with political natality and plurality
description: Trained directly under Martin Heidegger at Marburg, Hannah Arendt broke decisively with his solitary Dasein and withdrawal from politics, grounding the human condition instead in natality, plurality, and shared public action.
dialecticalTension: Confronts existential phenomenology's solitary concern with mortality against the public world of plural political beginnings.
historicalContext: Formulated across The Human Condition (1958) and Arendt's post-war political essays in dialogue with Being and Time.

citations.author: Hannah Arendt
citations.quote: Since action is the political activity par excellence, natality, and not mortality, may be the central category of political, as distinguished from metaphysical, thought.

label: Revived Aristotelian praxis and bios politikos for modern political theory
description: Arendt drew upon Aristotle's distinction between praxis (action in the polis) and poiesis (fabrication) to diagnose how modern mass society reduces civic freedom to economic labor.
dialecticalTension: Reclaims classical political action as an end in itself against modern instrumentalist and bureaucratic politics.
historicalContext: Central architectural scaffold of The Human Condition (1958).

citations.author: Dana Villa
citations.work: Arendt and Heidegger: The Fate of the Political

label: Critiqued Marx's elevation of labor over political action
description: While respecting Marx's analysis of alienation, Arendt argued that Marx collapsed genuine political action and fabrication into biological labor (animal laborans) and deterministic historical necessity.
dialecticalTension: Questions whether emancipatory politics can be reduced to socio-economic metabolism without eroding civic plurality.
historicalContext: Detailed in Chapter III ('Labor') of The Human Condition (1958) and On Revolution (1963).

label: Shaped communicative power and democratic public sphere theory
description: Arendt's conception of power as collective concert among speaking equals directly informed Jürgen Habermas's theory of communicative action and deliberative democracy.
dialecticalTension: Transforms Arendt's agonistic civic republicanism into a procedural discourse ethics of rational consensus.
historicalContext: Engaged extensively by Habermas in 'Hannah Arendt's Communications Concept of Power' (1977) and Between Facts and Norms (1992).

citations.author: Jürgen Habermas
citations.work: Hannah Arendt's Communications Concept of Power
